title: 2024–2027 multi-year budget presented, with 10.3% tax increase
subtitle: Police, library and county homelessness funding questions, deferred capital projects, and a November 22 workshop on possible reductions.
overview: Council held a special meeting to receive staff's proposed 2024–2027 multi-year budget. Staff presented a 2024 property tax levy increase of 10.3%, falling to 6.6% by 2027. The budget has three parts: city-controlled services, outside boards and agencies, and a new group of provincial impacts covering housing legislation, homelessness and the hospital commitment. Staff said they deferred over $690 million in capital work to limit the increase, and warned that deeper cuts to infrastructure renewal risk asset failures.

Council questioned the police, the library and the county's social services on their requests. A councillor moved to ask staff and outside boards to find a 2% reduction before the November 15 public delegation night. Concerns about timing and the lack of direction led the mover to withdraw it, and no vote was taken on it.

In its place, Council directed staff to schedule a budget workshop on November 22 at 6 pm to consider options for reductions. That motion passed {{vote:m2}}. Possible amendments will follow on November 29, after public delegations on November 15. Residents can also use the online engagement site and the public Budget Board for questions.

decisions.detail: Council directed staff to schedule a budget workshop on November 22 at 6 pm to consider further options for reductions, to inform possible budget amendments on November 29 {{vote:m2}}.

debate: Staff said the 10.3% reflects constraints beyond local control, including provincial housing legislation that reduces development charge revenue, county homelessness costs and the hospital commitment. The mayor said these provincial impacts are non-discretionary and set the starting point for the budget.

Staff cautioned that capital funding is already about 60% below the ideal level and that further cuts would mean more project reductions and possible asset failures. Several councillors questioned deferrals such as the York Road widening and downtown streetscaping, asking what deferral would cost later.

Councillors asked the police and library whether they could take a second look at their budgets. The police service said its request phases in staffing over four years and supports staff on trauma-related leave. The library said hiring ahead of the new central library is needed so it is ready to open.

A county representative said homelessness demand is rising, with shelters turning people away and more families affected. The county said the requested funding is the minimum needed for the next two years.

On the proposed 2% reduction, opponents said staff had spent months on the budget and that cuts are Council's decision. They also said a week was too short, and that the outside boards had already approved their budgets. Supporters said households face a heavy burden. Staff proposed a workshop that weighs options by community value instead of a percentage target.
